symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of units in the fixed finite population.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: The maximum cardinality of an active treatment interaction, with \(1\le\beta\le n\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: The rollout has \(k+1\) measurements including the baseline and terminal budget fraction.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: The largest treated fraction observed during the rollout.

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: The interior rollout fraction in the three-unit quadratic witness.

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: The smallest operationally permitted gap between consecutive rollout fractions.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The declared radius of the aggregate coefficient ellipsoid.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: The nominal error probability for the finite-sample Chebyshev confidence set.

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: \(U=(U_i)_{i\in I_n}\) is the sole source of design randomness.

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: A generic first scalar rollout fraction.

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: A generic second scalar rollout fraction.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: \(Y=(Y_i)_{i\in I_n}\) is fixed before \(U\) is drawn.

symbols.name: omega
symbols.def: \(\omega=(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_\beta)\) specifies the allowed aggregate energy at each interaction order.

symbols.name: C_CEY
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}\) is the degree-at-most-\(\beta\) class in CortezEichhornYu2022.

symbols.name: C_ellip
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\) contains the low-order schedules whose aggregate coefficient vector obeys \(a^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a\le B^2/n\).

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q\) is the explicit orthogonal transform obtained from the harmonic inclusion decomposition of subset levels \(1,\ldots,\beta\); \(Q_h\) denotes its lift for isotypic order \(h\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: \(H_h(p,w)\) is the \(h\)-th diagonal block of \(Q^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}Q\), restricted to the nonempty subset levels.

symbols.name: V_rob
symbols.role: robust variance bound and design criterion

assumptions.condition: The schedule \(Y\) is fixed before the draw of \(U\), and all probability statements condition on \(Y\).
The coordinates \((U_i)_{i\in I_n}\) are independent \(\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) variables and \(Z_i(r)=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le r\}\) for every \(r\in[0,1]\).
For every \(i\in I_n\) and \(z\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(Y_i(z)=c_{i,\varnothing}+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j\).
The aggregate coefficient vector satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a\le B^2/n\).

novel.justification: This permutation-invariant energy restriction models platforms with many weak interactions whose root-mean-square aggregate strength is stable within each interaction order. It contains dense exchangeable spillovers, sparse local interactions, and mixtures across every order up to \(\beta\), while allowing the order weights to be calibrated from domain bounds or a pilot ramp.

definitions.name: Published low-order schedule class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}=\{(Y,c):Y_i(z)=c_{i,\varnothing}+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j\text{ for every }i\in I_n\text{ and }z\in\{0,1\}^n\}\).

definitions.name: Ellipsoidal common-uniform coefficient class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)=\{(Y,c)\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}:a_S=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_n}c_{i,S}\text{ for every }S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta},\ a^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a\le B^2/n\}\).

definitions.name: Exact common-uniform covariance operator
definitions.construction: For \(S,T\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\), set \(K_{st}(S,T)=\min(p_s,p_t)^{|S\cap T|}p_s^{|S\setminus T|}p_t^{|T\setminus S|}-p_s^{|S|}p_t^{|T|}\) and \(G(p,w)_{S,T}=\sum_{s,t=0}^kw_sw_tK_{st}(S,T)\).

definitions.name: Design-computable radius-based variance certificate
definitions.construction: Given the implemented \((p,w)\), compute every reduced covariance block from the known common-uniform kernel and set \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=B^2n^{-1}\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}\). The certificate uses the declared radius and the known design, not observed outcomes.

definitions.name: Subset-lattice spectral equioscillation handle
definitions.construction: Start from the \(S_n\)-isotypic block decomposition of \(\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}\); impose the polynomial exactness equations on \(w\); quotient common covariance-null weight directions; then combine recession analysis, active-block KKT conditions, eigenvalue subgradients, and endpoint equioscillation to test joint attainment and characterize an attaining pair or a feasible sequence converging to the infimum together with a matching global dual certificate.

statements.statement: For every finite \(n\), \(1\le\beta\le n\), positive \(B\), and positive order weights \(\omega\), \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\subsetneq\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}\). Strictness is witnessed by the published-class schedule \(c_{i,\{1\}}=2B\sqrt{\omega_1/n}\) for every \(i\in I_n\), with all other coefficients zero: its nonzero aggregate coefficient satisfies \(a_{\{1\}}=2B\sqrt{\omega_1/n}\) and hence \(a^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a=4B^2/n>B^2/n\).
statements.justification: This records exactly what transfers from the published low-order model and prevents an ellipsoidal achievability result from being presented as a theorem for the full bounded-outcome class.
statements.gap: CortezEichhornYu2022 works with low-order schedules and coefficient-size bounds but does not isolate the permutation-invariant aggregate ellipsoid used by the exact covariance saddle.
statements.consumer: A reader can identify which parts of the design certificate remain valid when platform-specific coefficient bounds replace the ellipsoid.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(1\leq\beta\leq n\), \(B>0\), and \(\omega\in(0,\infty)^\beta\).  If \((Y,c)\in\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\), then the defining membership condition in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ellipsoidal\text{-}coefficient\text{-}class}\) includes \((Y,c)\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}\).  Hence
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\subseteq\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}.
\]

It remains to prove that the inclusion is strict.  Because \(1\leq\beta\leq n\), one has \(1\in I_n\) and \(\{1\}\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\).  For every \(i\in I_n\), define coefficients by
\[
c^*_{i,\{1\}}=2B\sqrt{\frac{\omega_1}{n}},
\qquad
c^*_{i,R}=0
\quad\text{for every }R\in\{\varnothing\}\cup\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\text{ with }R\neq\{1\},
\]
and define the associated potential outcomes by the low-order expansion
\[
Y_i^*(z)=c^*_{i,\varnothing}+
\sum_{R\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c^*_{i,R}
\prod_{j\in R}z_j,
\qquad z\in\{0,1\}^n.
\]
Thus \((Y^*,c^*)\) satisfies Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}low\text{-}order\text{-}schedule}\), and the membership criterion in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}low\text{-}order\text{-}class}\) gives
\[
(Y^*,c^*)\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}.
\]

By the definition of the aggregate coefficients, for \(R\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\),
\[
a_R^*=\frac1n\sum_{i\in I_n}c^*_{i,R}
=
\begin{cases}
2B\sqrt{\omega_1/n},&R=\{1\},\\
0,&R\neq\{1\}.
\end{cases}
\]
Every \(\omega_r\) is positive, so the diagonal matrix \(\Omega\) is invertible and \((\Omega^{-1})_{R,R}=\omega_{|R|}^{-1}\).  Consequently,
\[
(a^*)^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a^*
=\sum_{R\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}
\frac{(a_R^*)^2}{\omega_{|R|}}
=\frac{\left(2B\sqrt{\omega_1/n}\right)^2}{\omega_1}
=\frac{4B^2}{n}.
\]
Since \(B>0\) and \(n\geq1\),
\[
\frac{4B^2}{n}>\frac{B^2}{n}.
\]
The witness therefore violates Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}aggregate\text{-}coefficient\text{-}ellipsoid}\), equivalently the ellipsoid membership condition in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ellipsoidal\text{-}coefficient\text{-}class}\), and hence
\[
(Y^*,c^*)\notin\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega).
\]
The displayed witness belongs to the published class but not to the ellipsoidal class, which, together with the first inclusion, proves
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\subsetneq
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}.
\]

statements.statement: For every \(S,T\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) and stages \(s,t\), \[\operatorname{Cov}_U\!\left(\prod_{i\in S}Z_i(p_s),\prod_{j\in T}Z_j(p_t)\right)=K_{st}(S,T).\] Consequently, \(\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a\) for every low-order schedule.
statements.justification: This is the first changed proof step relative to spacing envelopes and independent-stage calculations: overlap cardinalities determine every cross-stage term exactly.
statements.gap: The variance proof of CortezEichhornYu2022 bounds these terms by local overlap and unit magnitudes; it does not state the full subset-intersection kernel.
statements.consumer: The kernel is the input required by a rollout scheduler to compare candidate ramps using their actual shared-hash dependence.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(S,T\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) and write \(X_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}Z_i(r)\).  By ass:common-uniform-rollout, the coordinates of \(U\) are independent and \(\Pr_U(U_i\le r)=r\).  Hence
\[
\mathbb E_U X_S(p_s)=p_s^{|S|}.
\]
For a coordinate in \(S\cap T\), the product of its two indicators is
\[
\mathbf 1\{U_i\le p_s\}\mathbf 1\{U_i\le p_t\}
=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le \min(p_s,p_t)\}.
\]
Coordinates in \(S\setminus T\) and \(T\setminus S\) occur at only one of the two stages.  Independence across coordinates therefore gives
\[
\mathbb E_U\{X_S(p_s)X_T(p_t)\}
=\min(p_s,p_t)^{|S\cap T|}p_s^{|S\setminus T|}p_t^{|T\setminus S|}.
\]
Subtracting \(\mathbb E_U X_S(p_s)\mathbb E_U X_T(p_t)=p_s^{|S|}p_t^{|T|}\) proves the displayed covariance formula in the statement, which is exactly \(K_{st}(S,T)\) by def:exact-covariance-operator.

By ass:low-order-schedule and the definition of \(a\), finite summation over units yields, for every \(r\in[0,1]\),
\[
M(r)=\bar c_{\varnothing}+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_SX_S(r),
\qquad
\bar c_{\varnothing}=\frac1n\sum_{i\in I_n}c_{i,\varnothing}.
\]
Consequently, def:rollout-estimator gives
\[
\widehat\tau_{p,w}
=\bar c_{\varnothing}\sum_{t=0}^kw_t
+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_S\sum_{t=0}^kw_tX_S(p_t).
\]
The first term is nonrandom.  Bilinearity of covariance, the already proved monomial covariance identity, and the finiteness of \(\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) now imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
&=\sum_{S,T}a_Sa_T\sum_{s,t=0}^kw_sw_tK_{st}(S,T)\\
&=\sum_{S,T}a_SG(p,w)_{S,T}a_T
=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a,
\end{aligned}
\]
where the second equality is def:exact-covariance-operator.  This proves both claims.

statements.statement: Because \(\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}\) depends on \((S,T)\) only through \((|S|,|T|,|S\cap T|)\), there is an explicit orthogonal subset-lattice transform that block diagonalizes it into isotypic blocks \(H_h(p,w)\), \(h=0,\ldots,\beta\), with block dimension at most \(\beta-h+1\). Each entry of \(H_h(p,w)\) is a finite sum of binomial coefficients and the kernel values \(K_{st}(S,T)\), and \[\lambda_{\max}\{\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}\}=\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}.\]
statements.justification: The reduction converts an operator indexed by all subsets of up to \(\beta\) units into a collection of small matrices without discarding covariance compatibility.
statements.gap: Neither Kallus2021 nor ChenLiDengWang2023 has the cross-level subset-intersection symmetry created by nested low-order monomials.
statements.consumer: A platform can evaluate and globally optimize the robust risk for small \(\beta\) without forming a matrix whose dimension grows as \(n^\beta\).
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(\mathcal X_r=\{S\subseteq I_n:|S|=r\}\).  For \(0\le j\le r\le n\), let \(R_{rj}\) be the inclusion matrix with rows indexed by \(\mathcal X_r\), columns indexed by \(\mathcal X_j\), and entries
\[
(R_{rj})_{S,A}=\mathbf 1\{A\subseteq S\}.
\]
These matrices are explicit finite zero--one matrices.  For every admissible \(r,\ell,j\), direct counting gives
\[
(R_{rj}R_{\ell j}^{\mathsf T})_{S,T}
=\binom{|S\cap T|}{j}.
\tag{1}
\]

We first give a self-contained orthogonal decomposition for these incidence matrices.  Define the down operator \(D_j=R_{j,j-1}^{\mathsf T}\), the up operator \(U_j=R_{j+1,j}\), and
\[
\mathcal L_0=\mathbb R,
\qquad
\mathcal L_h=\ker(D_h)\quad (h\ge1).
\]
If \(f\) is a function on \(\mathcal X_j\), then counting separately the term that leaves a set unchanged and the terms that exchange one element proves
\[
D_{j+1}U_jf-U_{j-1}D_jf=(n-2j)f.
\tag{2}
\]
Iterating (2) shows the following three facts.  For \(0\le h\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), \(f,g\in\mathcal L_h\), and \(h\le r\le n-h\),
\[
\langle R_{rh}f,R_{rh}g\rangle
=\binom{n-2h}{r-h}\langle f,g\rangle;
\tag{3}
\]
the lifted spaces arising from distinct values of \(h\) are orthogonal; and
\[
\mathbb R^{\mathcal X_r}
=\bigoplus_{h=0}^{\min(r,n-r)}R_{rh}\mathcal L_h.
\tag{4}
\]
For completeness, the induction step is obtained by taking the inner product of (2) with a vector in \(\ker D_j\); it gives injectivity of \(U_j\) when \(j<n/2\) and the squared-norm multiplier \(n-2j\).  Applying the same step successively from level \(h\) to level \(r\), and using \(R_{rh}=U_{r-1}\cdots U_h/(r-h)!\), gives (3).  Orthogonality follows by moving the down operators to the other side of the inner product, where they annihilate the harmonic vector.  Finally, rank--nullity applied at each step gives
\(\dim\mathcal L_h=\binom nh-\binom n{h-1}\); summing these dimensions over \(h\le\min(r,n-r)\) gives \(\binom nr\), proving (4).

Set \(d_h=\dim\mathcal L_h\), and choose an orthonormal basis \(e_{h,1},\ldots,e_{h,d_h}\) of each \(\mathcal L_h\).  By (3)--(4), the vectors
\[
q_{r,h,j}
=\binom{n-2h}{r-h}^{-1/2}R_{rh}e_{h,j},
\qquad
h\le r\le \min(\beta,n-h),
\tag{5}
\]
over all admissible \((r,h,j)\), form an orthonormal basis of the direct sum of the nonempty subset levels \(1,\ldots,\beta\).  Thus (5) constructs the orthogonal transform \(Q\) in the statement using only finite incidence matrices and orthonormal bases of explicit null spaces.

Let
\[
A=\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}.
\]
By def:exact-covariance-operator, \(G(p,w)_{S,T}\) depends on \((S,T)\) only through \((|S|,|T|,|S\cap T|)\); multiplication by \(\Omega^{1/2}\), whose diagonal entry on level \(r\) is \(\sqrt{\omega_r}\), preserves this property.  Therefore the level-
\((r,\ell)\) part of \(A\) has entries \(\phi_{r\ell}(|S\cap T|)\) for an explicitly known function \(\phi_{r\ell}\).  Define the forward difference by \((\Delta f)(c)=f(c+1)-f(c)\).  The finite Newton expansion
\[
\phi_{r\ell}(c)
=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(r,\ell)}(\Delta^j\phi_{r\ell})(0)\binom cj,
\qquad 0\le c\le\min(r,\ell),
\tag{6}
\]
and (1) express this level block as a finite linear combination of \(R_{rj}R_{\ell j}^{\mathsf T}\).

The scalar action needed to diagonalize (6) is also explicit.  If \(f\in\mathcal L_h\), repeated use of (2), or equivalently a direct count followed by the cancellation \(D_hf=0\), gives
\[
R_{\ell j}^{\mathsf T}R_{\ell h}f
=\begin{cases}
0,&j<h,\\
\displaystyle\binom{n-h-j}{\ell-j}R_{jh}f,&h\le j\le\ell.
\end{cases}
\tag{7}
\]
The second coefficient can be checked without any representation-theoretic premise: since
\(R_{\ell j}R_{jh}=\binom{\ell-h}{j-h}R_{\ell h}\), taking the inner product with \(R_{jh}f\) and using (3) gives
\[
\frac{\binom{\ell-h}{j-h}\binom{n-2h}{\ell-h}}
{\binom{n-2h}{j-h}}
=\binom{n-h-j}{\ell-j}.
\]
Writing \(\gamma_{r\ell j}=(\Delta^j\phi_{r\ell})(0)\), equations (6)--(7) and the identity
\(R_{rj}R_{jh}=\binom{r-h}{j-h}R_{rh}\) now yield
\[
A_{r\ell}R_{\ell h}f
=\left\{
\sum_{j=h}^{\min(r,\ell)}
\gamma_{r\ell j}
\binom{n-h-j}{\ell-j}
\binom{r-h}{j-h}
\right\}R_{rh}f.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus each matrix in (6) preserves the harmonic order and acts independently of the harmonic basis index; distinct harmonic orders are orthogonal by (4).  Hence \(Q^{\mathsf T}AQ\) is block diagonal.  For fixed \(h\), its nonzero level coordinates are indexed by
\[
\mathcal R_h=\{r:1\le r\le\beta,\ h\le r\le n-h\},
\]
so the corresponding block \(H_h(p,w)\) has size \(|\mathcal R_h|\le\beta-h+1\) and is repeated \(d_h\) times.  Orders with \(\mathcal R_h=\varnothing\) contribute no block.  Equations (1), (5), and (8) also show directly that every block entry is a finite sum of binomial coefficients and the quantities
\(\sqrt{\omega_r\omega_\ell}\sum_{s,t}w_sw_tK_{st}(S,T)\).  Thus the entries have exactly the computable form asserted in the statement.  Orthogonal similarity preserves eigenvalues, and repeated blocks do not change their maximum, so
\[
\lambda_{\max}(A)
=\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}.
\]
This completes the reduction.

statements.statement:
For every feasible \((n,\beta,k,q,\delta,B,\omega)\) with \(1\le\beta\le n\),
\[
\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}\sup_{(Y,c)\in\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)}\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=\frac{B^2}{n}\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\]
For every fixed \((p,w)\), if \(v^*\) is a unit leading eigenvector in an active block and \(Q_h\) is its explicit subset-lattice lift, then \(a^*=(B/\sqrt n)\Omega^{1/2}Q_hv^*\) attains the inner supremum. The schedule \(c^*_{i,S}=a^*_S\), \(c^*_{i,\varnothing}=0\), and \(Y_i^*(z)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c^*_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j\) satisfies \(\max_{i\in I_n,z\in\{0,1\}^n}|Y_i^*(z)|\le\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}|a_S^*|<\infty\) and is a legal least-favourable member of \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\). For fixed nodes \(p\), the weight problem has a semidefinite epigraph and attains its value after quotienting the common null directions of the covariance blocks.  The joint node--weight minimum is attained for every declared feasible tuple.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it solves Nature's exact common-uniform covariance problem, jointly minimizes over nodes and weights with guaranteed attainment, and produces the required legal converse schedule.
statements.gap: CortezEichhornYu2022 and the accepted Chebyshev-envelope proposal provide upper bounds without an attainable-covariance characterization or a joint-attainment proof; Kallus2021 provides an eigenvalue minimax template but not the nested subset kernel or rollout-node optimization.
statements.consumer: LinkedIn-style shared-hash ramps obtain a directly computable attained minimum and worst-case precision certificate under a declared interaction-strength budget.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a feasible \((n,\beta,k,q,\delta,B,\omega)\).  Every \(\omega_d\) is positive, so \(\Omega\) is positive definite.  For fixed \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\) and \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), define
\[
A(p,w)=\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2},
\qquad b=\Omega^{-1/2}a.
\]
Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}aggregate\text{-}coefficient\text{-}ellipsoid}\) is exactly
\[
\|b\|_2^2=a^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a\le \frac{B^2}{n}.
\tag{11}
\]
By Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\),
\[
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a=b^{\mathsf T}A(p,w)b.
\tag{12}
\]
The matrix \(A(p,w)\) is positive semidefinite, because the right side of (12) is a variance for every aggregate vector \(a\), and every such vector is realized by the fixed coefficient array \(c_{i,S}=a_S\).  The finite-dimensional Rayleigh quotient and (11) give
\[
\sup_{\|b\|_2^2\le B^2/n}b^{\mathsf T}A(p,w)b
=\frac{B^2}{n}\lambda_{\max}\{A(p,w)\}.
\tag{13}
\]

The supremum in (13) is attained by a legal schedule.  By Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}subset\text{-}lattice\text{-}block\text{-}reduction}\), choose an active block \(h\), a unit leading eigenvector \(v^*\) of \(H_h(p,w)\), and its unit orthogonal lift \(Q_hv^*\).  Put
\[
a^*=\frac B{\sqrt n}\Omega^{1/2}Q_hv^*.
\tag{14}
\]
Orthogonality of the lift yields
\[
(a^*)^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a^*=\frac{B^2}{n},
\qquad
(a^*)^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a^*
=\frac{B^2}{n}\lambda_{\max}\{A(p,w)\}.
\tag{15}
\]
For every \(i\in I_n\), define
\[
c^*_{i,S}=a^*_S,
\qquad c^*_{i,\varnothing}=0,
\qquad
Y_i^*(z)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a^*_S\prod_{j\in S}z_j.
\tag{16}
\]
The array (16) is fixed before \(U\), as required by Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}finite\text{-}population}\), and has degree at most \(\beta\), as required by Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}low\text{-}order\text{-}schedule}\).  Its aggregate coefficient is \(n^{-1}\sum_i c^*_{i,S}=a^*_S\), and (15) verifies the ellipsoid condition.  Since \(n\) and \(\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) are finite and every coordinate of \(a^*\) is real,
\[
\max_{i\in I_n,\ z\in\{0,1\}^n}|Y_i^*(z)|
\le\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}|a^*_S|<\infty.
\tag{17}
\]
Thus (16) belongs to Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ellipsoidal\text{-}coefficient\text{-}class}\) and attains (13).

Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}subset\text{-}lattice\text{-}block\text{-}reduction}\), Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}variance\text{-}certificate}\), and Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}saddle}\) now imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\inf_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}
  \inf_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}
  \sup_{(Y,c)\in\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)}
  \operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})\\
&\qquad=\frac{B^2}{n}
\inf_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}
\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}
=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]

We next prove that the joint infimum in (18) is attained.  The node class is nonempty because \(p_t=tq/k\) is feasible when \(\delta\le q/k\), and for every feasible \(p\) its nodes are distinct.  Since \(k\ge\beta\), the \((\beta+1)\)-row Vandermonde matrix on those nodes has full row rank, so \(\mathcal W_\beta(p)\) is nonempty.  Thus the value in (18) is finite.

Let \((p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})\) be a joint minimizing sequence.  For \(1\le j\le k\), put \(r_j^{(\ell)}=\sum_{t=j}^kw_t^{(\ell)}\).  The exact singleton identity in Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}rollout\text{-}budget\text{-}elbow}\), followed by the coordinate Rayleigh quotient, gives
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})
\ge \frac{B^2\omega_1\delta}{n}
\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j^{(\ell)}-1)^2.
\tag{19}
\]
The left side is bounded along a minimizing sequence.  Since \(B>0\), \(\omega_1>0\), and \(\delta>0\), all the tail sums \(r_j^{(\ell)}\) are uniformly bounded.  The identities
\[
w_k^{(\ell)}=r_k^{(\ell)},
\qquad
w_j^{(\ell)}=r_j^{(\ell)}-r_{j+1}^{(\ell)}\ (1\le j<k),
\qquad
w_0^{(\ell)}=-r_1^{(\ell)}
\tag{20}
\]
where the last follows from \(\sum_tw_t^{(\ell)}=0\), show that \(w^{(\ell)}\) is uniformly bounded.  The node polytope \(\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\) is closed and bounded in finite dimension, hence compact.  After taking a subsequence, \((p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})\to(p^*,w^*)\).  The polynomial exactness equations and node inequalities are closed, so \(p^*\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\) and \(w^*\in\mathcal W_\beta(p^*)\).  The kernel entries are continuous in \(p\), including across the diagonal because \(\min(\cdot,\cdot)\) is continuous; finite sums, matrix eigenvalues, and multiplication by \(w\) preserve continuity.  Therefore
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^*,w^*)
=\lim_{\ell\to\infty}V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})
=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\tag{21}
\]
Combining (13)--(18) with (21) replaces both joint infima in (18) by minima and proves the asserted joint attainment.

For completeness, fix \(p\) and expose the promised computable semidefinite epigraph.  Let \(d=|\mathcal S_{n,\beta}|\), and let \(\mathbb K(p)\) be the block matrix indexed by \((s,S)\) and \((t,T)\), with entry \(K_{st}(S,T)\).  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\) identifies \(\mathbb K(p)\) as a covariance matrix, so \(\mathbb K(p)\succeq0\).  Define
\[
D_p(w)b=(w_0\Omega^{1/2}b,\ldots,w_k\Omega^{1/2}b)^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
L_p(w)=\mathbb K(p)^{1/2}D_p(w).
\]
Direct block multiplication gives
\[
A(p,w)=D_p(w)^{\mathsf T}\mathbb K(p)D_p(w)
=L_p(w)^{\mathsf T}L_p(w).
\tag{22}
\]
Let \(C(p)_{r,t}=p_t^r\) for \(0\le r\le\beta\), and let \(e=(0,1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}\).  The weight constraints are \(C(p)w=e\).  Completing the square in a quadratic form shows directly that
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\rho I_d&L_p(w)^{\mathsf T}\\
L_p(w)&I_{(k+1)d}
\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\rho I_d-L_p(w)^{\mathsf T}L_p(w)\succeq0.
\tag{23}
\]
Indeed, the quadratic form at \((x,y)\) equals
\(x^{\mathsf T}\{\rho I_d-L_p(w)^{\mathsf T}L_p(w)\}x+
\|y+L_p(w)x\|_2^2\).  By (22), the fixed-node epigraph is therefore the semidefinite system
\[
C(p)w=e,
\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}
\rho I_d&L_p(w)^{\mathsf T}\\
L_p(w)&I_{(k+1)d}
\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
\tag{24}
\]
whose entries are affine in \((w,\rho)\).  Fixed-node attainment follows either from the joint sublevel argument (19)--(20) with \(p\) fixed, or after quotienting by the common null space \(\mathcal N_p=\ker\{w\mapsto L_p(w)\}\): the objective is constant on its cosets, and (19)--(20) provide a bounded representative for every feasible objective sublevel.  A convergent subsequence remains feasible by closedness of (24) and attains the fixed-node value.  This proves the semidefinite and attainment assertions without claiming the still-open global analytic node certificate.

statements.statement: For the schedule in \(\text{def:quadratic-witness}\), \[\Gamma(u,v)=\operatorname{Cov}_U\{M(u),M(v)\}=\frac{\min(u,v)^2-u^2v^2}{9}.\] The nonbaseline interpolation weights are \(w_x=-\{x(1-2x)\}^{-1}\) and \(w_{1/2}=4(1-x)/(1-2x)\), and \[\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=\frac{4(1-x)}{9(1-2x)}.\] This risk is strictly increasing on \([1/8,3/8]\), with values \(14/27\) at \(x=1/8\) and \(2/3\) at \(x=1/4\).
statements.justification: The witness verifies that exact shared-randomizer covariance changes the design criterion and that a familiar interior node need not dominate a more asymmetric node.
statements.gap: Published rollout bounds do not contain a legal finite-population example with a strict node-risk ordering generated by cross-stage covariance.
statements.consumer: A design reviewer can use this calculation as a regression test that implementation code has not silently replaced shared-hash stages by independent assignments.
statements.proof_tex:
Under def:quadratic-witness,
\[
M(r)=\frac13 Z_1(r)Z_2(r).
\]
By ass:common-uniform-rollout, or by lem:common-uniform-monomial-covariance with \(S=T=\{1,2\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma(u,v)
&=\frac19\left[\mathbb E_U\{Z_1(u)Z_2(u)Z_1(v)Z_2(v)\}-u^2v^2\right]\\
&=\frac19\left\{\min(u,v)^2-u^2v^2\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
Let the weights at \(x\) and \(1/2\) be \(w_x\) and \(w_{1/2}\).  The degree-one and degree-two equations in def:unbiased-weight-class are
\[
xw_x+\frac12w_{1/2}=1,
\qquad
x^2w_x+\frac14w_{1/2}=1.
\]
Their determinant is \(x(1-2x)/4>0\) for \(x\in[1/8,3/8]\), so their unique solution is
\[
w_x=-\frac1{x(1-2x)},
\qquad
w_{1/2}=\frac{4(1-x)}{1-2x}.
\tag{18}
\]
The remaining equation uniquely sets \(w_0=-w_x-w_{1/2}\); it contributes no random term because \(M(0)=0\).

Using (17) at the three required pairs gives
\[
9\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
=w_x^2(x^2-x^4)
+2w_xw_{1/2}\frac{3x^2}{4}
+w_{1/2}^2\frac3{16}.
\]
Substitution of (18) and collection over \((1-2x)^2\) give
\[
9\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
=\frac{1-x^2-6x(1-x)+3(1-x)^2}{(1-2x)^2}
=\frac{4(1-x)}{1-2x}.
\tag{19}
\]
Thus the asserted variance formula follows.  Its derivative on the specified interval is
\[
\frac{d}{dx}\frac{4(1-x)}{9(1-2x)}
=\frac4{9(1-2x)^2}>0,
\]
so it is strictly increasing.  Direct evaluation of (19) gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})\big|_{x=1/8}=\frac{14}{27},
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})\big|_{x=1/4}=\frac23.
\]
This proves the proposition and also verifies the smallest-instance arithmetic over the common-uniform design.

statements.statement: For every \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), and \((Y,c)\in\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\), \[\mathbb E_U[\widehat\tau_{p,w}]=\tau,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})\le V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w).\] If \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)>0\), then for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \[\Pr_U\!\left\{|\widehat\tau_{p,w}-\tau|\le\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)/\alpha}\right\}\ge1-\alpha,\] equivalently \(\Pr_U\{\tau\in\mathrm{CI}^{\mathrm{Ch}}_{1-\alpha}(p,w)\}\ge1-\alpha\). If \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=0\), then \(\widehat\tau_{p,w}=\tau\) almost surely and the singleton interval \(\{\widehat\tau_{p,w}\}\) has coverage one.
statements.justification: The same exact covariance support function used for design yields assumption-free finite-sample inference over the declared coefficient class.
statements.gap: CortezEichhornYu2022 gives spacing-based variance control for nested rollouts but does not turn the exact common-uniform covariance support function into a radius-certified finite-sample confidence set.
statements.consumer: The owner of a shared-hash production ramp can report a valid finite-sample interval using only the declared robustness radius and the implemented nodes and weights.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a feasible \((p,w)\) and a schedule in def:ellipsoidal-coefficient-class.  The expansion used in lem:common-uniform-monomial-covariance and ass:common-uniform-rollout give
\[
\mathbb E_U M(r)=\bar c_{\varnothing}
+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_Sr^{|S|}.
\tag{20}
\]
By def:unbiased-weight-class, \(\sum_tw_t=0\) and
\(\sum_tw_tp_t^d=1\) for every \(1\le d\le\beta\).  Applying these equalities term by term to (20) yields
\[
\mathbb E_U\widehat\tau_{p,w}
=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_S.
\tag{21}
\]
On the other hand, ass:low-order-schedule gives the finite-population causal contrast
\[
\tau
=\frac1n\sum_{i\in I_n}\{Y_i(\mathbf1)-Y_i(\mathbf0)\}
=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_S.
\tag{22}
\]
Equations (21)--(22) establish design unbiasedness without identifying \(\tau\) by definition.

By lem:common-uniform-monomial-covariance,
\[
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a.
\]
Applying the ellipsoid support calculation (7)--(9) from thm:exact-covariance-saddle, followed by lem:subset-lattice-block-reduction and def:variance-certificate, gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
\le\frac{B^2}{n}\lambda_{\max}\{\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}\}
=V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w).
\tag{23}
\]

Suppose first that \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)>0\), and put
\(R=\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)/\alpha}\).  For
\(X=\widehat\tau_{p,w}-\tau\), equations (21)--(22) give \(\mathbb E_UX=0\), while (23) gives \(\mathbb E_UX^2\le V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)\).  The pointwise inequality
\[
X^2\ge R^2\mathbf1\{|X|>R\}
\]
therefore implies
\[
\Pr_U(|X|>R)
\le\frac{\mathbb E_UX^2}{R^2}
\le\alpha.
\]
Taking complements proves the stated probability bound, and def:chebyshev-interval makes it equivalent to coverage by \(\mathrm{CI}^{\mathrm{Ch}}_{1-\alpha}(p,w)\).

If \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=0\), (23) gives \(\mathbb E_UX^2=0\).  Since \(X^2\ge0\), this implies \(X=0\) almost surely.  Hence \(\widehat\tau_{p,w}=\tau\) almost surely and the asserted singleton has coverage one.

statements.statement: Characterize every jointly minimizing node--weight pair for \(V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}\) by explicit necessary-and-sufficient global active-block conditions and a matching dual certificate over both nodes and weights. Determine the nondegenerate region of \((\beta,k,q,\delta,\omega)\) on which shifted Chebyshev--Lobatto nodes attain the minimum, are strictly suboptimal, or tie with other designs. The resolution must specialize at \((n,\beta,k,q)=(3,2,2,1/2)\) consistently with \(\text{prop:quadratic-witness}\).
statements.justification: Existence of a joint minimizer is settled; the genuinely open content is an analytic global certificate identifying all minimizers and the Chebyshev--Lobatto regime frontier.
statements.gap: No located result supplies necessary-and-sufficient active-block conditions or a global node dual certificate for this common-uniform saddle.
statements.consumer: Rollout designers obtain a reusable rule for when classical Chebyshev spacing is justified and when exact shared-hash covariance requires different nodes.

statements.statement:
For every declared feasible tuple and every \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), define \(r_j=\sum_{t=j}^kw_t\).  For every singleton \(S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\),
\[
G(p,w)_{S,S}=\sum_{j=1}^k(p_j-p_{j-1})(r_j-1)^2+(1-q)
\ge\delta\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2
\quad\text{and}\quad
G(p,w)_{S,S}\ge\frac{1-q}{q}.
\]
Consequently, if \(0<q<1\), then
\[
V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}\ge
\frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\frac{1-q}{q}.
\]
At \(q=1\), \(V^*_{n,\beta,k,1,\delta}=0\), attained by \(w_0=-1\), \(w_k=1\), and zero intermediate weights.  If \(\beta=1\), then for every \(0<q\le1\),
\[
V^*_{n,1,k,q,\delta}=\frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\frac{1-q}{q},
\]
and, for every fixed feasible \(p\), the unique minimizing weights are \(w_0=-1/q\), \(w_k=1/q\), and \(w_t=0\) for \(0<t<k\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a declared feasible tuple and \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\).  For a singleton \(S=\{i\}\), define
\[
f(u)=\sum_{t=0}^k w_t\mathbf 1\{u\le p_t\},
\qquad
r_j=\sum_{t=j}^k w_t\quad(1\le j\le k),
\qquad r_{k+1}=0.
\]
The exactness equations in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}unbiased\text{-}weight\text{-}class}\) give
\[
\mathbb E_U f(U_i)=\sum_{t=0}^k w_tp_t=1.
\tag{1}
\]
The separation condition in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}feasible\text{-}node\text{-}class}\) gives \(p_j-p_{j-1}\ge\delta>0\).  Apart from interval endpoints, which have uniform probability zero, \(f(U_i)=r_j\) when \(U_i\in(p_{j-1},p_j]\), and \(f(U_i)=0\) when \(U_i\in(q,1]\).  By Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}rollout}\), equation (1), and direct integration,
\[
\begin{aligned}
G(p,w)_{S,S}
&=\operatorname{Var}_U\{f(U_i)\}\\
&=\int_0^1\{f(u)-1\}^2\,du\\
&=\sum_{j=1}^k(p_j-p_{j-1})(r_j-1)^2+(1-q)\\
&\ge \delta\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The first equality is also the singleton case of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\).

There is a second lower bound which is sharp.  Since \(f=0\) off \([0,q]\), Cauchy--Schwarz for the ordinary Lebesgue integral gives
\[
1=\left\{\int_0^q f(u)\,du\right\}^2
\le q\int_0^q f(u)^2\,du.
\]
Thus \(\mathbb E_U f(U_i)^2\ge q^{-1}\), and (1) implies
\[
G(p,w)_{S,S}=\operatorname{Var}_U\{f(U_i)\}
\ge \frac1q-1=\frac{1-q}{q}.
\tag{3}
\]
Because \(S\) is a singleton, the corresponding diagonal entry of \(\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}\) is \(\omega_1G(p,w)_{S,S}\).  The Rayleigh quotient evaluated at the coordinate vector indexed by \(S\), (3), Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}variance\text{-}certificate}\), and Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}saddle}\) yield, for \(0<q<1\),
\[
V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}
\ge \frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\frac{1-q}{q}.
\tag{4}
\]

Suppose next that \(q=1\).  For any feasible node vector take
\[
w_0=-1,\qquad w_k=1,\qquad w_t=0\quad(0<t<k).
\tag{5}
\]
For each \(1\le d\le\beta\), \(p_0^d=0\) and \(p_k^d=1\), so (5) belongs to \(\mathcal W_\beta(p)\).  Every nonempty monomial equals zero at \(p_0=0\) and one almost surely at \(p_k=1\).  Its weighted readout is therefore constant, so \(G(p,w)=0\) and \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=0\).  Nonnegativity of a variance certificate gives
\[
V^*_{n,\beta,k,1,\delta}=0.
\tag{6}
\]

Finally suppose \(\beta=1\).  The interaction subsets are the singletons.  If \(S\ne T\), then \(S\cap T=\varnothing\), and the formula in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}covariance\text{-}operator}\) gives \(K_{st}(S,T)=p_sp_t-p_sp_t=0\).  All diagonal entries of \(G(p,w)\) equal \(\operatorname{Var}_U\{f(U_i)\}\), while \(\Omega=\omega_1I\).  Hence
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=\frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\operatorname{Var}_U\{f(U_i)\}.
\tag{7}
\]
For every feasible \(p\), the endpoint weights
\[
w_0=-q^{-1},\qquad w_k=q^{-1},\qquad w_t=0\quad(0<t<k)
\tag{8}
\]
belong to \(\mathcal W_1(p)\) and give \(f(u)=q^{-1}\mathbf 1\{u\le q\}\) almost everywhere.  Therefore their variance is \((1-q)/q\).  Equations (3) and (7) prove
\[
V^*_{n,1,k,q,\delta}=\frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\frac{1-q}{q}
\qquad(0<q\le1).
\tag{9}
\]
To prove uniqueness, equality in the Cauchy--Schwarz step above holds only when \(f\) is constant almost everywhere on \([0,q]\).  Its integral is one, so the constant must be \(q^{-1}\).  Every interval \((p_{j-1},p_j]\) has positive length, and hence \(r_j=q^{-1}\) for all \(j\).  Since \(w_k=r_k\), \(w_j=r_j-r_{j+1}\) for \(1\le j<k\), and \(w_0=-r_1\) by \(\sum_tw_t=0\), the weights in (8) are the unique minimizer for every fixed feasible \(p\).
statements.justification: This is the sharp rollout-budget obstruction and its exact first-order solution; it also supplies the coercivity needed for joint node--weight attainment.
statements.gap: Spacing-only envelopes do not expose the exact support restriction induced by a common-uniform ramp or the resulting unique first-order readout.
statements.consumer: A rollout designer can read off the unavoidable precision loss from stopping at fraction \(q<1\), and can implement the unique optimal first-order weights.

statements.proof_tex:
Define the displayed robust criterion using the published schedule class from Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}low\text{-}order\text{-}class}\).  Fix \(0<q<1\), a feasible \(p\), and \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\).  Because \(\beta\ge1\), \(\{1\}\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\).  For each \(A\in\mathbb R\), set
\[
c^{(A)}_{i,\{1\}}=A\quad(i\in I_n),
\qquad
c^{(A)}_{i,R}=0\quad
\text{for }R\in\{\varnothing\}\cup\mathcal S_{n,\beta},\ R\ne\{1\},
\]
and let \(Y_i^{(A)}(z)=Az_1\).  This is a degree-one, hence degree-at-most-\(\beta\), fixed schedule, so Assumptions~\(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}finite\text{-}population}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}low\text{-}order\text{-}schedule}\) and the published-class definition show that \((Y^{(A)},c^{(A)})\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}\) for every finite \(A\).

For this schedule, \(M(r)=AZ_1(r)\), and therefore
\[
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
=A^2G(p,w)_{\{1\},\{1\}}
\ge A^2\frac{1-q}{q},
\tag{10}
\]
where the equality follows from Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}rollout\text{-}estimator}\) and Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\), and the inequality is Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}rollout\text{-}budget\text{-}elbow}\).  Since \((1-q)/q>0\), letting \(|A|\to\infty\) in (10) proves that the inner supremum is \(+\infty\) for every feasible \((p,w)\).  Taking the two infima leaves it equal to \(+\infty\).

If \(q=1\), choose the endpoint weights \(w_0=-1\), \(w_k=1\), and zero intermediate weights.  As verified in Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}rollout\text{-}budget\text{-}elbow}\), these weights are polynomial-exact for every order up to \(\beta\).  Under the common-uniform design, \(Z(0)=\mathbf0\) and \(Z(1)=\mathbf1\) almost surely.  Consequently, for every fixed finite schedule in the published class,
\[
\widehat\tau_{p,w}=M(1)-M(0)
=\frac1n\sum_{i\in I_n}\{Y_i(\mathbf1)-Y_i(\mathbf0)\}=\tau
\quad\text{almost surely},
\]
so its design variance is zero.  Variances are nonnegative; hence the displayed minimax value is zero.  The divergence in (10) uses precisely the absence of a common coefficient or outcome radius.  It therefore does not apply to a subclass with a uniform \(Y_{\max}\) bound, nor does it make a claim about additional graph or observation-noise restrictions in the full published model.
statements.justification: This separates the exact full published schedule-envelope conclusion from the finite-radius ellipsoidal minimax theorem.
statements.gap: Without an explicit common radius, the broad polynomial schedule union has no finite robust precision guarantee below full rollout.
statements.consumer: Platform users learn exactly when a coefficient or outcome scale restriction is mathematically necessary for robust rollout design.

sampling_model.design: Finite-population common-uniform nested Bernoulli rollout: draw independent \(U_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) once and set \(Z_i(p_t)=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le p_t\}\) at every stage.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units and all potential outcomes are fixed; the assignment path is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is absorbing across the ordered fractions \(0=p_0<\cdots<p_k=q\).
sampling_model.overlap: No inverse exposure probabilities are used; implementability is enforced by \(p_t-p_{t-1}\ge\delta\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no sampled-law nuisance functions. The declared values \(B\) and \(\omega\), together with the known assignment law, determine the design-computable radius-based variance certificate.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 2 and 3 on pp. 5--6 establish unbiased polynomial-interpolation TTE estimators and spacing-based variance bounds for staggered Bernoulli and complete rollouts.
The mixed-strategy optimal design minimizes a largest-eigenvalue worst-case variance criterion over an ellipsoidal conditional-mean class.
The proposed single-stage network design optimizes an MSE upper bound through the covariance matrix of a cluster treatment vector.

tldr: A monotone production ramp assigns unit \(i\) at every fraction by the same threshold rule \(Z_i(u)=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le u\}\). Over the declared permutation-invariant ellipsoid for aggregate coefficients of a \(\beta\)-order finite-population schedule, the exact cross-stage covariance is a subset-intersection kernel rather than the diagonal or total-variation envelope used in existing rollout bounds. The kernel reduces the exponentially large robust eigenvalue to \(\beta+1\) subset-lattice isotypic blocks and turns joint node-and-weight choice into an exact spectral infimum problem. A leading eigenvector gives an explicit legal finite-valued least-favourable schedule for every fixed design. The same design-computable radius certificate yields a finite-sample Chebyshev confidence interval without a central limit theorem or an outcome-estimated variance. The open problem is attainment and an analytic characterization of optimal nodes, including the regime in which Chebyshev nodes cease to be optimal for the true common-uniform covariance.

project_justification.gap: Cortez, Eichhorn, and Yu derive polynomial-interpolation estimators for nested Bernoulli rollouts and control their variance by spacing bounds, while the accepted Chebyshev-envelope result optimizes a positive-semidefinite diagonal envelope. Neither result characterizes the covariance matrices attainable when every stage thresholds the same unit uniforms, and neither supplies a least-favourable legal schedule for that covariance.
project_justification.niche: The common-uniform path imposes exact intersection-cardinality identities across stages and interference monomials. Those identities create a robust design problem that is neither classical independent-error polynomial design nor a free positive-semidefinite covariance envelope.
project_justification.fill: The project identifies the exact monomial covariance kernel, exploits permutation symmetry to reduce the robust covariance operator to small subset-lattice blocks, formulates the joint rollout-node and polynomial-exact-weight infimum, constructs the least-favourable schedule from the active block eigenvector, and derives a finite-sample Chebyshev interval from the design-computable radius certificate.

related_work: CortezEichhornYu2022 is the setup and writing anchor. Its Theorems 2 and 3 on pp. 5--6 show unbiasedness and spacing-based variance bounds for polynomial interpolation under monotone Bernoulli and complete rollouts; the Bernoulli proof bounds each cross-stage monomial covariance rather than retaining its exact common-uniform value. Kallus2021 is the minimax-design method exemplar: its mixed-strategy optimal design reduces an ellipsoidal outcome adversary to a largest-eigenvalue criterion, but its design variable is a two-arm assignment law rather than nested rollout nodes and readout weights. ChenLiDengWang2023 makes assignment covariance a design variable under one-hop interference, but optimizes an upper bound for a single-stage Horvitz--Thompson estimator and explicitly notes that covariance feasibility is delicate. EichhornKhanUganderYu2024 treats low-order outcomes under general and clustered designs and gives design-dependent variance bounds, but does not characterize common-uniform cross-stage covariance or optimize rollout nodes. XuChenFernandezSinnoBhasin2015 and LiJamkhandeKochetkovLiu2022 document that production experimentation platforms use shared deterministic hashes to preserve assignment as traffic ramps; their balance diagnostics do not characterize interference-induced cross-threshold covariance. The exact-covariance Chebyshev question in the accepted CausalSmith proposal \(\texttt{exp\_rollout\_chebyshev\_minimax}\) is the immediate in-repository opening, and this paper addresses its missing attainable-covariance and converse-schedule steps on a declared aggregate-coefficient ellipsoid.
technical_internal_limitation: The permutation-invariant aggregate-coefficient ellipsoid is a strict subclass of the unrestricted bounded \(\beta\)-order schedules used for the broadest variance bounds in CortezEichhornYu2022. It is selected because it is rich enough to retain every interaction order and overlap pattern while admitting an exact spectral adversary and an explicit least-favourable schedule. Exact minimax optimality over the full product \(\ell^1\) coefficient class remains open. The \(N=3\) calculation proves only that common-uniform covariance changes node rankings relative to an independent-stage surrogate; it does not identify a design attaining the robust infimum.
honest_scope: The exact covariance identity, subset-lattice reduction, ellipsoidal minimax infimum, fixed-design least-favourable construction, and finite-sample robust coverage are theorem targets only over \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\), not over the full published low-order class. Joint node--weight attainment and a necessary-and-sufficient frontier for Chebyshev optimality are open. A design-based central limit theorem is outside the formal claims because pairwise non-independence does not supply a genuine setwise dependency graph. When \(\beta=1\), the block system reduces to the linear-rollout variance expressions associated with Theorems 2 and 3 of CortezEichhornYu2022 on pp. 5--6. When \(q=1\), the target is observed at the endpoint and the design reduces to the no-extrapolation estimator \(M(1)-M(0)\).
